description: How to create custom Claude Code skills — education module for AIOS reports

sections.title: What Are Skills?
sections.content: Skills are reusable Claude Code commands that encode your business processes. Instead of explaining the same workflow every time, you teach Claude once and use a slash command from then on.
examples: /onboard-client — runs your entire client onboarding checklist
/prep-meeting — generates a briefing doc before any client meeting
/weekly-report — compiles your weekly team report from all your tools
/generate-invoice — creates an invoice from your time tracking data

sections.title: Anatomy of a Skill
sections.content: A skill is a markdown file in your Claude Code project that describes the workflow. Claude reads it and executes the steps.
sections.example_skill:
# /prep-meeting

Prepare a client meeting briefing.

## Prerequisites
- CRM connected via MCP
- Calendar connected via MCP
- Client context files in memory/clients/

## Parameters
- --client: Client name
- --date: Meeting date

## Steps
1. Look up the client in CRM via MCP
2. Read client context file from memory/clients/{client-slug}.md
3. Check calendar for meeting details and attendees
4. Pull recent communications (last 30 days)
5. Compile briefing with: client overview, recent activity, open items, talking points

## Output
A briefing document saved to meetings/{date}-{client}.md

sections.title: Building Your First Skill
sections.content: Start with your most repetitive task — the one you do every week that follows the same pattern.
process: Identify a repetitive workflow (something you do 4+ times/month)
Write down the exact steps you follow
Note which tools you touch at each step
Test with a real case and refine
tips: Start simple — your first skill should have 3-5 steps
Use existing MCP connections — don't build new integrations just for one skill
Include error handling — what if the CRM lookup returns no results?
Test with edge cases — what about a new client with no history?
Iterate — skills get better with use, update them as you learn

sections.title: Skill Library Best Practices
sections.content: As you build more skills, organize them into a library your whole team can use.
practices: Document each skill with examples and prerequisites
Version your skills in git so changes are tracked
Review skills quarterly — remove unused ones, update outdated ones
Let team members propose new skills based on their pain points
